clue.text: Pasty, etc, going off in pigeonhole

indicators.note: food going off turns bad, so the letters of the first two words are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A batch of pasties and similar snacks spoiling in a small storage compartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' and 'pigeonhole' both look like nouns from a kitchen or office; the verb sense of 'pigeonhole' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeonhole an actor or anyone is to fix them in one narrow category, the verb's stereotyping sense.

clue.text: A man may wear one: soldiers sometimes button it

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, were part-time British soldiers
button it means be quiet, which sh also demands

explanation.surface: A uniform jacket that soldiers sometimes do up.
explanation.walkthrough: TASH is British slang for a moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: A moustache is facial hair that many men grow, so a man may wear one.

clue.text: Plain glass carriage

parts.note: a prairie is a wide grassy plain of North America
a schooner is a tall glass for sherry or beer

explanation.surface: A simple description of an unadorned glass coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie schooner was the covered wagon used by American pioneers, a horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: See surrounding area strike disaster

indicators.note: surrounding has the first piece wrapped round the rest

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, whose seat is a cathedral city
to lam is to beat or strike

explanation.surface: A warning that a strike in the surrounding district will be disastrous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is an ecclesiastical seat, not a command to look.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a catastrophe, an event causing great harm or distress.

clue.text: Burrows became hard to see: just the tops

parts.note: concrete or jelly sets when it becomes hard

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of a word is its first letter, so only those are taken

explanation.surface: Animal burrows set hard, so only their entrances are visible.
explanation.definitionFit: Badgers live in underground burrows called setts.

clue.text: Families departed — but not with us?

parts.note: the opposite of 'us' is 'them', in the us-and-them sense
OB, from Latin obiit, marks a death on gravestones and in records

explanation.surface: Relatives who have died are no longer with us, a gentle euphemism.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'not with us' a second euphemism for death; it really means the other side in an us-and-them divide.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is organised into crime 'families', so the gangland organisation collectively stands for those families.

clue.text: Cross and upset by horse getting shot

indicators.note: in a down entry upset turns the letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, which is called horse
getting shot of something means getting rid of it

explanation.surface: Someone angry and distressed because a horse has been shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but is a noun, a crossbreed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is the offspring of two different breeds or species, a cross between them.

clue.text: One supposedly recommending cake in slices transformed into meat-eater

indicators.note: slices means cuts into, so the short word sits inside the rearranged letters
transformed means changed in shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cake cut up and somehow turned into a carnivore.
explanation.walkthrough: She was said to have said 'Let them eat cake', hence 'supposedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French queen is famously credited, probably falsely, with telling starving peasants to eat cake.

clue.text: Temperance group force House to outlaw drug stores

parts.note: to ban something is to outlaw it

indicators.note: stores means holds within, so the drug contains the other letters

parts.note: dope is slang for a drug
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A temperance body pressing Parliament to ban drug shops.
explanation.definitionFit: The Band of Hope was a British Victorian society teaching children to abstain from alcohol.

clue.text: Good university's missing old master

indicators.note: missing means one letter is taken out

parts.note: virtuous means morally good
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A fine university has lost an Old Master painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old master' looks like one phrase, a painting, but 'old' gives O and 'master' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a master of an art, especially a brilliant musical performer.

clue.text: Mark left by limited old Greek composer

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: limited here means cut short, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: Attic is the ancient Greek dialect and people of Athens

explanation.surface: A scar left by some ancient Greek, seemingly a fragment of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark left by' reads as one phrase but gives three pieces; 'limited' trims ATTIC to ATTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Domenico Scarlatti was an Italian baroque composer famous for his keyboard sonatas.

clue.text: Cut narrator's unable to bear

indicators.note: a narrator speaks the words aloud, so the following synonym is given by its sound

parts.note: barren means unable to bear offspring or fruit

explanation.surface: A storyteller whose tale is trimmed and who cannot stand it any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb, but it is the definition: a baron of beef is a butcher's joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron of beef is a large joint made of both sirloins, so the word names a cut of meat.

clue.text: Tip for ironing skirt, black

indicators.note: the tip of a word here is its end, so the last letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: to skirt is to go round the edge, and an edge is a rim

explanation.surface: A household tip for pressing a black skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt' looks like a garment but works as a noun-like edge, the rim.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim and black both describe a bleak, dismal outlook, as in black or grim humour.

clue.text: Light scooter, if tested, keeps reversing

indicators.note: the held run is then read from right to left
the words keep the letters within them, a run spanning their middle

explanation.surface: A scooter under test keeps going backwards, with a light on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' reads as a scooter's lamp but is a verb, as in lighting a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To light something is to ignite it, and the phrasal verb means exactly to make it start burning.

clue.text: Pop big John on the wing, switching positions often

indicators.note: on the wing means in flight, so these letters fly about into a new order

explanation.surface: A big man named John playing on the wing keeps changing place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the wing' suggests football positions, which the definition also echoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving frequently from one job to another is the practice of changing employment positions often.

clue.text: Plain fellow meeting with champion too much

parts.note: overt means plain or openly visible
he stands for a male person, a fellow
the top person is the champion, the best

explanation.surface: An ordinary man meets a champion and finds it overwhelming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective for the fellow but supplies OVERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something over the top is excessive, an idiom from soldiers going over the trench parapet.

clue.text: One turning out lies about Gus, no longer with us?

definitions.text: One turning out lies about Gus, no longer with us?

indicators.note: turning means the letters are spun round into a new order
no longer with means lacking, so the letters of us are removed from the name

explanation.surface: A funeral speaker tells flattering untruths about the late Gus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer with us' strips US from GUS, leaving G; the whole clue also describes a funeral tribute.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who delivers praise of the dead at a funeral may well embellish the truth about them.

clue.text: Lot of cloth is here? Very little

definitions.meaning: the cloth is the clergy, and many of them are to be found in church
a tiny amount or distance, as in not giving way at all

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether the fabric is stocked here, and is told only a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cloth' is the clergy, as in a man of the cloth; CH is church.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a tiny distance, so the word stands for a very small amount, as in 'give an inch'.

clue.text: For one good with his fork, finally an alternative?

definitions.text: For one good with his fork, finally an alternative?

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cook handy with a fork is offered another tool to use.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints that a cook beating eggs with a fork has an alternative implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen whisk for beating eggs does the job a fork can do, so it is an alternative to it.

clue.text: Horse to kick stomach

definitions.meaning: a horse for ordinary riding, often one for hire
to kick an opponent's shins, as in football or rugby
to stomach something is to tolerate it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to make a horse kick another in the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: The one word covers a riding mount, a kick at the shins and putting up with something.

clue.text: O for one large pub, good or bad!

indicators.note: bad here means gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A cry about a big pub where the beer might be good or bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O' is the letter naming a blood type, not a zero or an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Type O is one of the ABO blood types, so O is an example of the category.

clue.text: Understood drink to be an unexpected snag

parts.note: got means understood, as in 'I got it'
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Someone realises a drink turned out to be a surprising problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'got you!' marks catching someone out, and the word is also a hidden trap or catch.

clue.text: See blocks with spikes extended

indicators.note: to block is to stand in the way, so one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: pronged means having prongs, sharp spikes
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at building blocks fitted with spikes, stretched out.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolonged means lengthened in time, drawn out, which is to be extended.

clue.text: ME port of call: capital

definitions.meaning: ME is the Middle East, and this Gulf port is a common stopover
it is the capital of the emirate of the same name

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern stopover described as excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf city is both a major Middle East port and airline hub and its own emirate's capital.

clue.text: Given time, current returns

indicators.note: returns signals coming back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: now means current, the present moment

explanation.surface: Given enough time, a flow of electricity or water comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' suggests electricity but means present.
explanation.definitionFit: Wont is an old adjective meaning accustomed, so being wont to do something is being given to it.

clue.text: Stole hit repeatedly heard on radio?

indicators.note: radio is only heard, so the synonym is given by its sound

parts.note: to rap is to knock or strike repeatedly

explanation.surface: A stolen hit record played over and over on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like the verb but is a noun, a shawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A stole is a long scarf or shawl worn round the shoulders, a kind of garment draped about one.

clue.text: King or queen deposed, meaning the opposite of order!

indicators.note: a deposed monarch is removed, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: ironic speech means the opposite of what it says
R stands for Rex, king, or Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A monarch overthrown, and the result is ironically chaos rather than order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is not tidiness but a classical architectural style.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of architecture, with scroll-shaped capitals, alongside Doric and Corinthian.

clue.text: Sentimental writer succeeded first in description of judge?

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the description

parts.note: the saying 'sober as a judge' supplies the word
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
1ST written with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: A journalist who followed on, first to describe a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: IST is 1ST, first, with the figure one as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob sister is a journalist, originally a woman, who writes tear-jerking human-interest stories.

clue.text: The Irish force people back, tease Welshman

indicators.note: back means the word runs backwards

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them
Dai is a typical Welsh man's name, short for David

explanation.surface: Irish police pushing a crowd back while mocking a Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garda Síochána is the Irish police, and its officers are collectively called by its plural form.

clue.text: One cheering team returning regularly in truck

indicators.note: in puts them inside the truck

parts.note: a pickup is a small open truck

indicators.note: returning reverses those picked letters
regularly takes every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A supporter cheers as their team rides back in a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of 'team' give EM, which 'returning' turns into ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick-me-up is a tonic or drink that revives the spirits, something that cheers.
